experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes. Witness breathtaking panoramic views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. This is the crown jewel of the region and a must-do for serious trekkers.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges in a stunning alpenglow display. The relatively short 2-day hike from Ghorepani makes it accessible yet profoundly rewarding.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and stunning views without the crowds of the main Annapurna circuit. Trek through dense forests of oak and rhododendron, alpine meadows, and high ridgelines with close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). A perfect off-the-beaten-path adventure for nature lovers.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk & Dal Bhat Experience
experiences.description: Hike through the traditional Gurung and Magar villages of the Annapurna foothills, learning about indigenous mountain culture, ancient customs, and local farming practices. Conclude the experience with an authentic Dal Bhat meal prepared by a local family — the staple trekker's fuel of lentil soup, rice, vegetables, and pickles, often served with unlimited refills.

experiences.name: Annapurna Circuit Partial Trek – Thorong La Pass Crossing
experiences.description: Tackle the legendary Thorong La Pass at 5,416m, the highest point of the Annapurna Circuit and one of the world's great high-altitude crossings. Trek through diverse ecosystems from subtropical forests to arid Tibetan-style plateaus, passing through Manang and descending into the sacred town of Muktinath. An epic physical and spiritual journey through the heart of the Himalayas.
experiences.location: Thorong La Pass, Manang to Mustang, Annapurna Circuit

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take a budget local bus or shared taxi to Thamel (Kathmandu's backpacker hub). Check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel (~$8-12/night). Rest and freshen up, then take a short walk around Thamel to get oriented, exchange currency at a local money changer for better rates, and pick up any last-minute trekking supplies from the many gear shops.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's vibrant streets, visit the nearby Kathmandu Durbar Square area for a quick evening glimpse. Arrange your onward bus ticket to Pokhara for the next morning at a local travel desk (tourist bus ~$10-12).

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Thamel restaurant (~$3-4)
meals.dinner: Budget thali or momo (dumplings) at a local Nepali restaurant in Thamel (~$4-5)

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize rest after your flight. Keep your valuables secure in Thamel. Book your tourist bus to Pokhara for Day 2 (departs ~7:00-8:00 AM). Confirm your accommodation booking for Pokhara/Annapurna region.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 6:00 AM. Board the tourist bus from Thamel to Pokhara (~7:00 AM departure, ~7-8 hour journey, $10-12). Enjoy scenic mountain and river valley views along the Prithvi Highway. Pack snacks for the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara around 2:00-3:00 PM. Check into a budget lakeside guesthouse near Phewa Lake (~$8-12/night). Take a short walk along the Lakeside promenade (Baidam) to get your bearings and enjoy views of the Annapurna range reflecting on the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Lakeside Bazaar for budget trekking gear rental if needed (trekking poles, sleeping bag liners). Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake from the shoreline. Register at the TIMS (Trekkers' Information Management System) counter and obtain your Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) — budget ~$30 USD total for permits.

meals.breakfast: Simple bread, eggs, and tea at a Thamel guesthouse or roadside stall (~$2)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the bus or a quick stop at a roadside dhaba (~$2-3)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with vegetables at a local Pokhara lakeside restaurant (~$3-5)

day_by_day.notes: The bus journey can be long and winding — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. Obtain your ACAP permit ($30) and TIMS card ($20) before heading to the trailhead. These are mandatory for trekking in the Annapurna region.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take a local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (the main trekking trailhead, ~1.5 hours, ~$3-4). Begin the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek from Nayapul. Trek through terraced rice fields and small Gurung and Magar villages to Tikhedhunga (~3 hours, 1,540m elevation).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m), a challenging but rewarding 45-minute steep climb with over 3,000 stone steps. Arrive in Ulleri and enjoy panoramic views of the Annapurna South and Hiunchuli peaks. Rest at a local teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a basic teahouse in Ulleri (~$3-5/night, often free or discounted if you eat meals there). Socialize with fellow trekkers and local teahouse owners. Enjoy the crisp mountain air and star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara guesthouse breakfast — porridge or eggs with tea (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~$4-5)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat set meal at the Ulleri teahouse (~$5-6) — unlimited refills are the trekker's tradition!

day_by_day.notes: Start trekking early to avoid afternoon heat and to have buffer time. The Ulleri staircase is steep — take it slow and stay hydrated. October is peak trekking season in Nepal with clear skies and excellent mountain views. Carry at least 2 liters of water.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wake-up to catch sunrise views of Annapurna South from Ulleri. Begin trekking through rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m), a popular stopping point (~3-4 hours of moderate trekking). The trail passes through dense forest with frequent bird sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani by midday. Drop your pack at a teahouse and take an optional short acclimatization hike around the village. Visit the local shops for postcards and snacks. Rest your legs and enjoy the views of Dhaulagiri (8,167m) — the world's 7th highest peak — and the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.evening: Optional: Attend a brief cultural interaction at the teahouse — many hosts share stories of local Gurung culture. Prepare your gear for the pre-dawn hike to Poon Hill the next morning. Early bedtime by 8:30-9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at Ulleri teahouse (~$3)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or noodle soup at a Ghorepani teahouse (~$4-5)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at the Ghorepani teahouse (~$5-6)

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani has many teahouses — negotiate a good rate, especially if you commit to eating all meals there. Set an alarm for 4:30 AM for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow. The village has basic charging facilities (~$1-2 per charge). Temperatures drop significantly at night — use your sleeping bag liner.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 4:30 AM. Hike up to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) with a headlamp — about 45 minutes to 1 hour of uphill trekking. Witness one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises with 360-degree panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Hiunchuli, and dozens of other Himalayan peaks bathed in golden light. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, continue the trek toward Tadapani (2,630m) via Deurali Pass. The trail passes through beautiful rhododendron forests (these bloom brilliantly in spring but are lush and green in October). Trek duration: approximately 4-5 hours with moderate difficulty.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tadapani and check into a teahouse. Enjoy stunning views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain, 6,993m) — one of Nepal's most iconic and sacred peaks that has never been officially summited. Relax and journal about the day's incredible experiences.

meals.breakfast: Hot lemon tea at Poon Hill, then full breakfast at Ghorepani teahouse — eggs, toast, and tea (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Snack at Deurali Pass — biscuits and chocolate carried from Pokhara, or simple teahouse soup (~$3-4)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with local vegetables at Tadapani teahouse (~$5-6)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is approximately $2 USD — pay at the gate. The sunrise is absolutely worth the early start. Bring warm layers as it will be very cold before dawn at 3,210m. The trail from Ghorepani to Tadapani can be muddy — trekking poles are very helpful.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike from Tadapani through dense rhododendron and bamboo forests descending to Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4-5 hours of trekking with some steep descents and ascents. Chhomrong is the last major village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary inner sanctum and is the gateway to the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into a teahouse. Chhomrong is a beautiful Gurung village with terraced fields and excellent views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Explore the village, visit the local Gurung Cultural Museum (small donation appreciated), and fill up water bottles (purification tablets recommended — saves money vs. buying bottled water).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a brief cultural demonstration or conversation with your teahouse host about Gurung traditions. Prepare for the more remote section of the trek ahead — stock up on snacks like energy bars, biscuits, and nuts from the village shops. Prices increase as you go higher.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or muesli with tea at Tadapani teahouse (~$3)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse along the trail (~$4-5)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with spinach and potato curry at Chhomrong teahouse (~$5-7)

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on snacks in Chhomrong as prices increase significantly above this point (sometimes 2-3x). Carry water purification tablets or a SteriPen to avoid buying expensive bottled water. The trail from Tadapani to Chhomrong involves a significant descent followed by a steep climb up to Chhomrong — take your time.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down the famous Chhomrong stone staircase, cross the Chhomrong Khola (river) on a suspension bridge, and begin ascending toward Sinuwa (2,360m). Continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m) — approximately 3-4 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery to Dovan (2,600m) and then to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) — approximately 2-3 more hours. The trail follows the Modi Khola river through a narrow gorge with towering walls on either side. The vegetation becomes more alpine as you gain altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — a cluster of lodges in a dramatic gorge setting. The sound of the rushing Modi Khola river provides a natural soundtrack. Acclimatization is important at this stage — do some light stretching and stay well hydrated.

meals.breakfast: Eggs on toast and tea at Chhomrong teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (great for altitude acclimatization) and bread at Bamboo teahouse (~$4-5)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or vegetable noodle soup at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~$6-8) — note prices are higher in the sanctuary

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is a local remedy widely believed to help with altitude acclimatization — order it at every meal from here onward. Avoid alcohol above Chhomrong. The gorge can be cold and damp even in October — have your rain jacket and warm layers accessible. Watch for landslide areas on the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through the narrowing Modi Khola gorge to Deurali (3,230m) — approximately 2 hours. The trail passes through areas prone to avalanche in winter but is safe in October. Continue to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) — approximately 2 more hours. The views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) become increasingly dramatic and close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp and take a well-deserved rest. The landscape transforms into a high-altitude glacial environment with moraines and the sacred Fishtail peak towering above. Spend the afternoon acclimatizing, taking short walks around MBC, and preparing mentally and physically for the push to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the extraordinary sunset alpenglow on the surrounding peaks — Machhapuchhre, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Hiunchuli — turning shades of orange, pink, and purple. The amphitheater of peaks surrounding the sanctuary is one of the most awe-inspiring sights in the Himalayas. Early to bed by 8:30 PM.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and ginger tea at Himalaya Hotel (~$4)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and chapati at Deurali teahouse (~$5-6)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse (~$7-9) — prices are at their highest here

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness can occur above 3,000m. Watch for symptoms: severe headache, nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite, or confusion. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink 3-4 liters of water daily. The temperature at MBC in October can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night — ensure your sleeping bag is rated for cold temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start at 5:00-5:30 AM. Trek from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m) — approximately 1.5-2 hours in the dark with headlamps to arrive for sunrise. The final approach crosses a glacial moraine and enters the sacred inner sanctuary. At ABC, you are surrounded by a 360-degree amphitheater of towering Himalayan giants: Annapurna I (8,091m — the world's 10th highest peak), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and the sacred Machhapuchhre. This is the highlight of the entire trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC soaking in the extraordinary views, taking photographs, and reflecting on the achievement of reaching this remote and sacred place. Explore the moraine and glacier edge areas (carefully and safely). Begin the descent back to MBC after lunch, then continue down to Deurali or Himalaya Hotel to sleep at a safer altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) after a long but exhilarating day. Celebrate your achievement with fellow trekkers. Your body will feel the relief of descending to a lower altitude.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at MBC before dawn departure, then a full breakfast at ABC teahouse after sunrise (~$5-6)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or garlic soup at ABC before descending (~$7-8)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat — a well-earned feast — at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~$6-8)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most important day of the trek. Start very early to catch the sunrise at ABC — it is absolutely spectacular. October weather is generally clear and stable, but always check with teahouse owners about conditions. Descending the same day from ABC to a lower altitude is strongly recommended to reduce altitude sickness risk. Take plenty of photos — this is a once-in-a-lifetime view.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent from Himalaya Hotel back through the gorge, passing Dovan, Bamboo, and Sinuwa. The descent is much faster than the ascent — approximately 4-5 hours to reach Chhomrong. Enjoy the changing vegetation as you descend from alpine to subtropical forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chhomrong. Take an alternative trail variant if desired — the route via New Bridge and Jhinu Danda (1,780m) is a popular option that adds a special reward: natural hot springs! Trek down to Jhinu Danda (approximately 1.5 hours from Chhomrong via New Bridge).
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot spring pools at Jhinu Danda on the banks of the Modi Khola river (~$3 entry fee). This is one of the most blissful experiences on the entire trek — soaking tired muscles in natural geothermal waters with jungle surroundings. Stay overnight at a Jhinu Danda teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Himalaya Hotel (~$4)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a Sinuwa or Chhomrong teahouse (~$5-6)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry and rice at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$5-6)

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a legendary trekker reward after days of hard trekking. The entry fee is approximately $3 USD. Bring a towel and flip-flops. The pools are open from morning until evening. This is a great place to meet other trekkers and share stories of the sanctuary.

day_by_day.morning: Morning soak in the hot springs (they open early — worth a pre-breakfast dip!). Then trek from Jhinu Danda down to New Bridge and continue toward Landruk (1,565m) or take a different return route via Tolka and Landruk — approximately 3-4 hours of pleasant downhill trekking through terraced farmland and traditional villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Landruk through Potana and Dhampus (1,650m) — a beautiful Gurung village with exceptional views of the Annapurna range and Machhapuchhre. Dhampus is one of the most photographed villages in the Annapurna foothills. Explore the village and interact with local Gurung families.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight at a Dhampus teahouse. Enjoy the final evening in the mountains with a magnificent sunset view of the Annapurna range from the village. Reflect on your incredible 9-day trekking journey through the sanctuary.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast with tea at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a Landruk teahouse (~$4-5)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with local seasonal vegetables at Dhampus teahouse (~$5-6)

day_by_day.notes: Dhampus is a popular day-hike destination from Pokhara, so you may encounter day-trippers. The village has a community homestay program — ask your teahouse host about local Gurung cultural experiences. This is your last night on the trail — savor the mountain atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the mountains — wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Annapurna range from Dhampus. Begin the descent to Phedi (1,130m) — approximately 2 hours of easy downhill trekking. From Phedi, take a local bus or shared taxi back to Pokhara (30-40 minutes, ~$2-3).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Pokhara — you've completed the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek! Check into your lakeside guesthouse. Treat yourself to a hot shower (luxury after days of cold mountain showers!). Take a relaxing boat ride on Phewa Lake (~$5-7 for a rowing boat rental) and paddle to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your trek with a lakeside dinner. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for a panoramic evening view of Pokhara, the lake, and the Annapurna range — accessible by a short hike or boat + hike combination. Browse the Lakeside market for souvenirs — Nepali handicrafts, thangka paintings, pashmina scarves.

meals.breakfast: Final mountain breakfast — porridge and tea at Dhampus teahouse (~$3)
meals.lunch: Celebratory dal bhat or momos at a Pokhara lakeside restaurant (~$4-5)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a lakeside restaurant — try Newari or Tibetan cuisine (~$7-10) to celebrate your achievement

day_by_day.notes: You can get a massage in Pokhara for ~$10-15/hour — highly recommended after 10 days of trekking! Get your trekking certificate from the ACAP office if desired (a nice memento). Return any rented gear to avoid extra charges. Book your bus back to Kathmandu for Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Pokhara. Visit the International Mountain Museum (entry ~$5) — an excellent museum dedicated to the history of Himalayan mountaineering, the eight-thousanders, and the cultures of mountain peoples. Well worth a few hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tourist bus back to Kathmandu (~7-8 hours, $10-12, departing around 7:00-8:00 AM — adjust morning activities accordingly, or take an afternoon departure at 1:00 PM and arrive evening). Alternatively, take a 25-minute domestic flight ($80-100 on Buddha Air or Yeti Airlines) for spectacular aerial views of the Himalayas — a budget splurge worth considering for the views alone. Check into a Thamel guesthouse upon arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Evening walk through Thamel. Visit Swayambhunath Stupa (the Monkey Temple) if arriving by bus with daylight remaining — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with panoramic city views. Enjoy a final Kathmandu evening meal in Thamel.

meals.breakfast: Lakeside cafe breakfast in Pokhara — pancakes or muesli with coffee (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Roadside dhaba stop on the bus journey or packed snacks (~$2-3)
meals.dinner: Tibetan restaurant in Thamel — try thukpa (noodle soup) or butter tea (~$5-7)

day_by_day.notes: If taking the morning bus, pack the night before and arrange a 6:30 AM checkout. The domestic flight option (Pokhara to Kathmandu) offers breathtaking aerial views of the Annapurna and Langtang ranges — if budget allows, this is a memorable experience. Book in advance as flights fill quickly in October peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kathmandu. Visit Pashupatinath Temple (the sacred Hindu cremation temple on the Bagmati River, UNESCO World Heritage Site — free to walk the outer areas, ~$5 for inner temple access) and Boudhanath Stupa (one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world, entry ~$3) — both are close together and reachable by taxi (~$5) or local bus (~$0.30).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Thamel for final souvenir shopping — Singing bowls, Thangka paintings, handmade paper products, pashmina scarves, and trekking gear are excellent value. Bargain respectfully. Pack your bags and head to Tribhuvan International Airport. Allow 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kathmandu — carry beautiful memories of the Annapurna Sanctuary, the world's greatest mountain panoramas, warm Nepali hospitality, and the achievement of one of the world's most iconic treks.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast — sel roti (traditional ring-shaped rice bread) with tea at a local Thamel bakery (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Last dal bhat at a Thamel local restaurant (~$3-4) — a fitting farewell to Nepal's national dish
meals.dinner: Airport meal or inflight meal

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 14 days: Accommodation $80-120, Meals $120-160, Transport $40-60, Permits $50, Activities/Entrance Fees $20-30, Gear/Misc $30-50. Total estimated budget: $340-420 USD for 14 days — very achievable for a budget-conscious trekker. Namaste and safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your hotel in Pokhara via private taxi or tourist bus (approximately 6–7 hours by bus or 25-minute flight). If flying to Pokhara, book an afternoon domestic flight. Settle into your accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Take a gentle stroll along Pokhara's Lakeside (Phewa Lake) promenade. Enjoy the calm atmosphere, browse local shops, and watch the sunset reflect off the lake with Annapurna peaks in the background.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick snack at Kathmandu airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or en route — try a local dal bhat set at a roadside dhaba for NPR 250–400
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moondance Restaurant, Lakeside Pokhara — try their pasta or Nepali thali set (mid-range, NPR 600–900 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or in Pokhara. Keep NPR cash handy as ATMs can be limited on the trail. Purchase a TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) in Pokhara before trekking begins.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) — hike up or take a boat across Phewa Lake and walk up for panoramic views of Pokhara, the lake, and the Annapurna range at sunrise. A perfect acclimatization walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office to obtain your ACAP permit and TIMS card if not done yet. Explore the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara to learn about Himalayan geography, flora, fauna, and mountaineering history.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Nepali cultural show at one of Pokhara's local cultural centers, or enjoy a relaxed evening at Lakeside. Pack your trekking gear and prepare for the trail starting tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a local café — try eggs, toast, and Nepali milk tea (NPR 300–500)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a lakeside café — try a Nepali set meal or momos (steamed dumplings) for NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dinner at Caffe Concerto or similar mid-range restaurant in Lakeside — try grilled fish or vegetable curry (NPR 700–1000)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your ACAP permit (NPR 3,000 per person) and TIMS card (NPR 2,000 for individual trekkers). Arrange transport to Nayapul or Phedi for the next morning. Stock up on snacks, water purification tablets, and any trekking supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours by jeep or local bus, approximately NPR 200–500). Begin trekking from Nayapul toward Tikhedhunga (1,540m), passing through terraced fields, small villages, and rhododendron forests. Trek duration: approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri (2,073m), famous for its long stone staircase of over 3,000 steps through dense forest. Arrive at Ulleri and check into a teahouse. Rest and explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the teahouse terrace with views of the surrounding hills. Interact with fellow trekkers and local teahouse owners. Enjoy the cool mountain air.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Pokhara hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Traditional Nepali dal bhat at your Ulleri teahouse — filling and nutritious for the trek ahead (NPR 500–700, often includes unlimited refills)

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek covers approximately 11 km with significant elevation gain. Pace yourself on the Ulleri stone steps — they are steep but manageable. Stay hydrated. October weather typically offers clear skies and cool temperatures — ideal trekking conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and trek from Ulleri to Ghorepani (2,874m) through beautiful rhododendron and oak forests. The trail is well-marked and moderately steep. Trek duration: approximately 3–4 hours. Arrive at Ghorepani and check into your teahouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and acclimatize at Ghorepani. Take a short exploratory walk around the village. Visit the local viewpoint for early afternoon views of Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna range. Set an alarm for a very early morning for Poon Hill the next day.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up by the teahouse fire with fellow trekkers. Share stories from the trail. The evenings in Ghorepani can be quite cold in October — layer up.

meals.breakfast: Porridge, eggs, and tea at your Ulleri teahouse before departure (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Soup and bread or fried rice at a teahouse en route to Ghorepani (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Pasta, vegetable curry, or dal bhat at your Ghorepani teahouse (NPR 500–800)

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani is one of the most popular stops on the Annapurna Circuit. Book your teahouse in advance during October (peak season). Temperatures can drop to near freezing at night — bring a warm sleeping bag liner.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 4:30 AM and hike 45 minutes to Poon Hill (3,210m) to witness one of Nepal's most iconic sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. The panoramic view includes Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Dhaulagiri. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) through dense rhododendron forest — stunning in October with clear skies. The trail offers continuous mountain views. Trek duration: approximately 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tadapani and settle into your teahouse. Enjoy the quieter atmosphere compared to Ghorepani. Watch the alpenglow on the peaks at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea or coffee at Poon Hill viewpoint (available from vendors), then a full breakfast back at the teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Light snack or noodle soup en route to Tadapani (NPR 350–550)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or vegetable stir fry at your Tadapani teahouse (NPR 500–750)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee: NPR 100. Bring a headlamp, warm layers, and your camera for sunrise. The Ghorepani–Tadapani trail passes through one of the finest rhododendron forests in Nepal — in October, the forest is lush green.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m), one of the gateway villages to the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail descends steeply through forests before crossing the Modi Khola river and climbing up to Chhomrong. Trek duration: approximately 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into your teahouse. Explore this charming Gurung village with its stone-paved lanes, terraced fields, and spectacular views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Chhomrong viewpoint for golden hour mountain views. Chat with local Gurung families and learn about their culture and traditions. Prepare mentally for the deeper sanctuary trek ahead.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or muesli with tea at your Tadapani teahouse (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried noodles at a teahouse en route or in Chhomrong (NPR 450–650)
meals.dinner: Nepali set meal at your Chhomrong teahouse — try the local garlic soup which is popular among trekkers for altitude (NPR 500–800)

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is the last village with reliable ATM access before the sanctuary. Withdraw sufficient cash here. The trail into the sanctuary beyond Chhomrong has no ATMs. Stock up on snacks and any personal supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down to Sinuwa (2,360m) via a steep descent to the Chhomrong Khola and then a steep climb back up. Continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m). Trek duration: approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Bamboo to Dovan (2,600m) through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery with the Modi Khola river rushing below. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary proper, with towering walls of rock and forest on all sides.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Dovan teahouse and rest. The isolation and raw natural beauty of this section is extraordinary. Listen to the river and observe the night sky — minimal light pollution makes for excellent stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at your Chhomrong teahouse before departure (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Simple noodle soup or dal bhat at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse (NPR 450–650)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse — options become simpler deeper in the sanctuary (NPR 500–800)

day_by_day.notes: The trail from Chhomrong into the sanctuary involves significant descent and re-ascent. Trekking poles are highly recommended. Watch for leeches in shaded forest sections — tuck trousers into socks. The sanctuary is a restricted zone — keep your ACAP permit accessible for checks.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) via Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) and Hinku Cave (3,170m). The landscape transforms dramatically as the valley opens up and the towering peaks of the Annapurna massif come into full view. Trek duration: approximately 5–6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp and check into your teahouse. Take time to acclimatize and absorb the awe-inspiring 360-degree mountain panorama. The sacred Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) towers directly above.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint the surrounding peaks in shades of gold, orange, and pink. The silence and grandeur of the high Himalaya at this elevation is deeply moving. Retire early as tomorrow's highlight requires an early start.

meals.breakfast: Toast, eggs, and tea at Dovan teahouse (NPR 450–700)
meals.lunch: Soup and bread or noodles at Himalaya Hotel teahouse en route (NPR 500–750)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or simple pasta at MBC teahouse — hot and hearty for the altitude (NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude at MBC is 3,700m — watch for signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness). Drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol, and ascend slowly. Diamox (acetazolamide) can be taken as a precaution — consult your doctor before the trip. Temperatures drop sharply at night.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 4:30 AM and trek from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m) in the dark with headlamps to arrive at sunrise. The final approach through the glacial moraine reveals the full amphitheater of the Annapurna Sanctuary — Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre surrounding you on all sides. A truly life-changing experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC — explore the base camp area, take photographs, and soak in the extraordinary environment. After lunch, begin the descent back to MBC or continue to Dovan depending on energy levels.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at MBC or Dovan. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers over a warm meal. Reflect on the achievement.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea or coffee and biscuits before the early morning hike to ABC; proper breakfast at ABC teahouse upon arrival — eggs, porridge (NPR 600–900 at this altitude)
meals.lunch: Simple noodle soup or instant noodles at ABC teahouse (NPR 600–900)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC or Dovan teahouse (NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130m is the highest point of this itinerary. Spend at least 2–3 hours here to fully appreciate the surroundings. The descent from ABC to MBC takes approximately 1.5 hours. If feeling strong, continue to Dovan to make the return journey more manageable. October typically offers excellent visibility at ABC.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent from Dovan (or MBC) back through the sanctuary. Trek to Bamboo or Sinuwa, retracing the trail through bamboo and rhododendron forest. The descent is significantly easier on the lungs but harder on the knees — use trekking poles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending to Chhomrong. Enjoy the return views of the Annapurna range from a different perspective. Check back into a teahouse in Chhomrong.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the successful Annapurna Sanctuary trek with a well-deserved hot shower (available in Chhomrong teahouses) and a hearty meal. Rest tired legs.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and tea at your starting teahouse before descent (NPR 500–750)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse (NPR 450–650)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly more varied menu at Chhomrong — try apple pie or a hot chocolate alongside your main meal (NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: The descent from the sanctuary involves the same steep sections encountered on the way up — take it slowly to protect your knees. Trekking poles and proper footwear are essential. You've now completed the core Annapurna Sanctuary trek — a major accomplishment.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back toward the lower trails. Descend to Jhinu Danda (1,780m), a small village famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. Trek duration: approximately 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon soaking in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs — the perfect remedy for sore trekking muscles. The hot springs are set in a beautiful riverside location. Continue trekking to New Bridge or Chomrong area for overnight.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the peaceful riverside setting. Enjoy the sounds of the Modi Khola and the relief of lower altitude. Prepare for the final trekking days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at your Chhomrong teahouse (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Light snack or noodle soup at Jhinu Danda (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or vegetable curry at your teahouse (NPR 500–750)

day_by_day.notes: Jhinu Danda hot springs entry fee: approximately NPR 200–300 per person. Bring a towel and change of clothes. The springs are a beloved highlight for returning trekkers. October temperatures make the hot springs especially enjoyable after the cold nights at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from the Chomrong/New Bridge area back to Nayapul via a lower trail route, passing through terraced farmland, small Gurung villages, and riverside paths. Trek duration: approximately 4–5 hours. Arrive in Nayapul and arrange jeep or bus transport back to Pokhara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Pokhara by early afternoon. Check back into your Pokhara hotel or guesthouse. Enjoy a long hot shower, laundry service, and the comforts of a proper hotel after days on the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your Annapurna trek with a special dinner at one of Pokhara's better restaurants. Enjoy a lakeside walk under the stars with the Annapurna range silhouetted in the distance.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your teahouse before the final trek day (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Meal at a local restaurant in Nayapul or en route to Pokhara (NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Pokhara's Caffe Concerto or The Lemon Tree — try wood-fired pizza, pasta, or a proper steak to reward yourself (NPR 800–1,400 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jeep from Nayapul to Pokhara costs approximately NPR 300–500 per seat in a shared vehicle. Book accommodation in Pokhara in advance as October is peak season. Consider a mid-range hotel with a mountain view room for the final Pokhara nights.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning in Pokhara. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a gentle boat ride on Phewa Lake — rent a rowing boat (NPR 400–600 per hour) and paddle to the Tal Barahi Temple on the lake's island. The reflection of Machhapuchhre in the lake is iconic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave near Davis Falls — an impressive cave system with a sacred Shiva shrine inside. Explore the colorful Lakeside bazaar and pick up trekking souvenirs, Nepali handicrafts, thangka paintings, or pashmina scarves as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset paragliding over Pokhara and Phewa Lake from Sarangkot — one of the world's best paragliding destinations. Tandem flights with certified operators cost approximately USD 80–100. Book in advance through a reputable operator.

meals.breakfast: Full Western or Nepali breakfast at your hotel or a lakeside café — treat yourself (NPR 500–800)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a lakeside restaurant — try Nepali-style buff (buffalo) momos or a fresh salad (NPR 500–750)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moondance or Busy Bee Café, Lakeside — enjoy live music if available and a relaxed final Pokhara evening (NPR 700–1,100)

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding is weather-dependent — October generally offers excellent conditions. Confirm your flight with the operator the evening before. Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave entry: approximately NPR 30–50 each. This is a wonderful recovery and exploration day after the intense trek.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. Wake early for one last sunrise view of the Annapurna range from your hotel or Lakeside. Pack your bags and check out. If time allows, visit the Bindabasini Temple — the main Hindu temple in Pokhara — for a cultural farewell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Pokhara Airport for a domestic flight to Kathmandu (25 minutes, approximately USD 80–120 one way). Upon arrival in Kathmandu, depending on your international departure time, visit Thamel for last-minute shopping or the famous Boudhanath Stupa or Pashupatinath Temple if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your international departure. Reflect on 14 extraordinary days in the Annapurna region — from Pokhara's lakeside to the high Himalayan sanctuary at 4,130m.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast at your Pokhara hotel — try sel roti (traditional ring-shaped rice bread) with yogurt and honey (NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Pokhara or Kathmandu airport, or at a Thamel restaurant if time allows — try a final dal bhat (NPR 400–700)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining on your departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your domestic flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu well in advance — October is peak season and flights fill quickly. Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for check-in and security at Kathmandu. Declare any cultural artifacts or large purchases at customs. Nepal allows export of items under 100 years old with a receipt.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to your boutique stay in the Annapurna Conservation Area. En route, stop at a scenic viewpoint above Pokhara to capture your first panoramic glimpse of the Annapurna massif. A personal guide will brief you on the 14-day journey ahead during the drive.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your boutique accommodation, enjoy a welcome drink and a curated orientation session with your head guide. Stroll the immediate lodge grounds as the alpenglow paints the peaks at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments provided in the private transfer vehicle — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and Nepali tea
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the lodge's candlelit dining pavilion: Nepali thali with organic dal bhat, seasonal vegetable curries, handmade achaar, and local Himalayan herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Acclimatization is key — rest well tonight. Altitude at base lodge is approximately 1,000–1,200 m. Hydrate generously and avoid alcohol on the first night.

day_by_day.morning: Guided nature walk through the subtropical forests surrounding the lodge. A naturalist guide identifies endemic flora and bird species including the Himalayan monal (Nepal's national bird). Walk duration approximately 2–3 hours at a gentle pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Gurung village near the trail base. Engage in a private cultural immersion session — learn about Gurung heritage, observe local weaving, and participate in a millet bread-making demonstration with village elders.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the lodge's mountain-view terrace led by a resident yoga instructor. Followed by a private stargazing experience with a telescope set up by the lodge's astronomy guide.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet lodge breakfast: freshly baked Nepali bread, Himalayan honey, seasonal fruit platter, eggs cooked to order, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Alfresco lunch in the Gurung village — authentic home-cooked meal featuring gundruk soup, sel roti, and fermented vegetables prepared by a local host family
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at the lodge: five-course dinner with Himalayan trout, wild mushroom risotto with Tibetan herbs, and a dark chocolate fondant with cardamom cream

day_by_day.notes: Light hiking shoes are sufficient today. Carry a reusable water bottle — the lodge provides filtered mountain spring water. Village visit requires modest clothing; scarves available at the lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the first trekking segment toward Ghandruk (1,940 m) — one of the largest Gurung settlements in Nepal. The trail winds through rhododendron and oak forests with sweeping views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Trek duration approximately 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghandruk and check into a premium teahouse suite. Explore the Ghandruk Eco-Museum, which documents the Gurung culture, traditional costumes, and the history of the Gurkha soldiers. A private guided tour is pre-arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Gurung cultural performance — traditional Ghatu dance and Rodhi folk music arranged exclusively for your group. Enjoy cocktails and local raksi (rice wine) on the teahouse rooftop overlooking the Annapurna range.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: buckwheat pancakes with wild berry compote, yogurt with Himalayan honey, and ginger lemon tea
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch prepared by the lodge chef: whole-grain wraps with smoked chicken, roasted vegetables, energy bars, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner: grilled yak steak with roasted potatoes, seasonal greens sautéed in garlic and butter, and warm apple cinnamon pudding

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is moderate. Trekking poles recommended. The trail gains approximately 700 m in elevation — pace yourself. October weather typically offers clear skies and temperatures between 10–18°C during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Early sunrise hike to a panoramic viewpoint above Ghandruk for unobstructed views of Annapurna South (7,219 m), Hiunchuli (6,441 m), and Machhapuchhre (6,993 m). Photography session with your dedicated guide who assists with framing and golden-hour composition tips.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend toward Chhomrong (2,170 m), a key gateway village to the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail passes through terraced farmland and suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river. Trek duration approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into a premium hilltop lodge. Enjoy a private hot stone bath (arranged by the lodge) and a therapeutic foot massage by a trained therapist brought in for your group.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast: Tibetan bread with yak butter and jam, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and black tea
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic lunch set up by your support team on the banks of the Modi Khola: artisan cheeses, cold cuts, crackers, fresh vegetables, and lemonade
meals.dinner: Chhomrong lodge dinner: slow-cooked lamb curry with saffron rice, lentil soup, pickled vegetables, and kheer (rice pudding) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The descent to Chhomrong involves stone staircases — knee support recommended. Leeches may be present on lower trails in October; gaiters provided by the guide team. Chhomrong marks the official entry point into the Annapurna Sanctuary restricted zone.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong toward Sinuwa (2,360 m) and onward to Bamboo (2,310 m). The trail descends steeply before climbing through dense bamboo groves and rhododendron forests. Wildlife spotting opportunities include red panda and Himalayan tahr. Trek duration approximately 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Bamboo camp and rest at a premium tented camp set up exclusively for your group along the riverbank. Afternoon birdwatching session with a specialist ornithologist guide identifying species unique to the Annapurna Conservation Area.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire evening under a canopy of stars in the gorge. Your private chef prepares a fireside dinner. A short guided meditation session is offered by the lodge's wellness guide to help with acclimatization and relaxation.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: oatmeal with dried fruits and nuts, banana pancakes, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels, trail mix, protein bars, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Exclusive campfire dinner: wood-fired whole chicken with herb marinade, roasted root vegetables, garlic naan, and warm brownie with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Temperature drops significantly in the gorge at night — sleeping bags rated to -10°C are provided. The bamboo section can be slippery; trekking poles essential. No mobile network from this point — satellite communication device carried by lead guide.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo through Dovan (2,600 m) and Himalaya Hotel (2,920 m). The trail narrows and ascends steeply through ancient forests draped in moss and lichen. The dramatic gorge walls begin to tower overhead. Trek duration approximately 5–6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel camp and rest. A private acclimatization briefing is held by your lead guide, covering altitude sickness prevention, hydration protocols, and the terrain ahead. Light stretching session led by the wellness guide.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at camp. Enjoy a private hot water bottle service in your tent and read about the Annapurna Sanctuary's geological history from curated books provided in your premium tent kit.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: scrambled eggs with herbs, toast with peanut butter and honey, seasonal fruit, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Dovan: dal bhat prepared by a local teahouse — hearty, authentic, and perfectly timed for mid-trek energy
meals.dinner: Camp dinner: hearty vegetable and chicken soup, pasta primavera with Himalayan herbs, garlic bread, and hot chocolate with marshmallows

day_by_day.notes: Altitude is now approaching 2,900 m. Watch for symptoms of AMS (headache, nausea, dizziness). Pulse oximeters are carried by the medical guide. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water today. No alcohol at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700 m. The landscape transforms dramatically — the gorge opens into a vast glacial amphitheater ringed by 7,000 m+ peaks. The iconic fishtail summit of Machhapuchhre dominates the skyline. Trek duration approximately 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC and acclimatize. Take a short exploratory walk around the base camp area to help the body adjust. Your guide shares the mythology and spiritual significance of Machhapuchhre — a peak considered sacred and never officially summited.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint the surrounding peaks in shades of amber, pink, and violet from MBC. A private photography guide assists with long-exposure and landscape shots. Hot drinks and snacks served at the viewing area.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: porridge with brown sugar and dried berries, boiled eggs, toast, and green tea
meals.lunch: Packed lunch consumed on the trail: energy-dense wraps with tuna, avocado, and cheese, plus chocolate and nuts
meals.dinner: MBC camp dinner: tomato basil soup, dal bhat with seasonal vegetables, and warm cinnamon apple dessert — all prepared by your private chef

day_by_day.notes: MBC sits at 3,700 m — acclimatization is critical. Sleep with your head slightly elevated. The temperature at night can drop to -5°C or below. Your premium tent includes a thermal lining and fleece sleeping bag. Tomorrow's push to ABC is the highlight of the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure (5:00 AM) from MBC to reach Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130 m for sunrise. The 2-hour ascent crosses glacial moraines and snowfields. Arriving at ABC as the first light illuminates the 360-degree amphitheater of Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at ABC. Explore the base camp area with your mountaineering guide who shares stories of historic Annapurna expeditions. A private picnic lunch is set up at a scenic spot within the sanctuary. Guided meditation session amid the peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Annapurna peaks transition through sunset colors — a phenomenon known locally as 'alpenglow.' Your photographer guide captures professional-quality portraits of you at ABC. Return to premium camp for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn energy breakfast at MBC: hot porridge, energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, and thermos of ginger lemon honey tea to carry
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic at ABC: smoked chicken sandwiches, fresh fruit, cheese selection, dark chocolate, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Celebratory ABC dinner: Nepali feast with dal bhat, chicken curry, seasonal vegetables, pickles, and warm gulab jamun for dessert — champagne toast with a non-alcoholic sparkling option available

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130 m is the highest point of this itinerary. If any guest shows signs of severe AMS, immediate descent protocol will be activated. Oxygen canisters are carried by the medical guide. This is the crown jewel of the trek — take your time and absorb every moment.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise at ABC before beginning the descent. A brief private ceremony is held — your guide offers a traditional Buddhist prayer and khata (white silk scarf) blessing for a safe descent. Begin trekking down toward MBC and continue to Deurali (3,230 m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent through the gorge, passing familiar landmarks now seen from a different perspective. The body feels noticeably lighter as altitude decreases. Arrive at Himalaya Hotel camp for an afternoon rest and hot shower (camp solar-heated water system).
day_by_day.evening: Reflective evening journaling session encouraged by your wellness guide. Share stories and highlights of the ABC experience over a relaxed fireside gathering with your guide team.

meals.breakfast: ABC camp breakfast: eggs Benedict with Himalayan herbs, toast, fruit, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: whole grain wraps, energy bars, mixed nuts, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Himalaya Hotel camp dinner: hearty lentil soup, grilled vegetable pasta, garlic bread, and rice pudding

day_by_day.notes: Descent is easier on the lungs but harder on the knees — trekking poles and knee braces recommended. The body will feel significantly better below 3,500 m. Spirits are typically high on descent days.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Himalaya Hotel through Dovan and Bamboo, retracing the ascent route. The familiar bamboo groves and rhododendron forests feel welcoming on the way down. Trek duration approximately 4–5 hours to Chhomrong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chhomrong. Enjoy a well-deserved private spa treatment at the lodge — deep tissue massage and aromatherapy using locally sourced Himalayan essential oils. Rest and recover in your premium room.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the Chhomrong lodge terrace with unobstructed views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Your guide presents a curated slideshow of professional photos taken throughout the trek.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: banana pancakes, fresh fruit, yogurt with honey, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Chhomrong teahouse lunch: vegetable noodle soup, spring rolls, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: pan-seared Himalayan trout with lemon butter sauce, roasted vegetables, mashed potatoes, and chocolate mousse for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Spa session is 90 minutes and should be booked in advance (pre-arranged by the trip coordinator). Laundry service available at Chhomrong lodge — fresh clothing for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back to Ghandruk via an alternative scenic route through Kimrong Khola valley. The trail offers different perspectives of the Annapurna range and passes through cardamom and millet farms. Trek duration approximately 4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghandruk. Private guided tour of the village's most photogenic corners — ancient stone houses, water mills, and terraced fields. Meet a local Gurung elder for a private storytelling session about Gurung mythology and Gurkha military history.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with your full guide and porter team in Ghandruk. A traditional Gurung blessing ceremony is performed. Cultural exchange and group celebration of the successful Annapurna Sanctuary trek.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: Tibetan bread with yak butter, boiled eggs, seasonal fruit, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Farmhouse lunch in Kimrong village: home-cooked dal bhat, fresh vegetables from the garden, and local herbal tea
meals.dinner: Gourmet farewell dinner at Ghandruk's best lodge: mixed grill platter with yak, chicken and lamb, roasted potatoes, salad, and traditional Nepali sweet — sikarni (spiced strained yogurt)

day_by_day.notes: This is the last night on the trail. Ensure all gear is packed and ready for the return journey tomorrow. Tips for guide and porter team are customary and deeply appreciated — suggested amounts provided in your trip welcome pack.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning photography walk around Ghandruk's rooftops and terraces for the last mountain sunrise of the trek. Then begin the descent toward Nayapul via Kimche, through lush subtropical forest and terraced fields. Trek duration approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury vehicle picks up the group at Nayapul and transfers to Pokhara (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into a premium lakeside resort on Phewa Lake — a dramatic contrast to the mountain camps. Enjoy the resort's infinity pool overlooking the lake and the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride on Phewa Lake in a private wooden boat, drifting past the reflection of Machhapuchhre in the still water. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the lake island. Return for a lakeside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Ghandruk lodge breakfast: eggs to order, toast, fresh fruit platter, and green tea
meals.lunch: Pokhara lakeside restaurant lunch: grilled fish tacos, fresh salad, and mango lassi upon arrival in the city
meals.dinner: Pokhara fine dining: rooftop restaurant with lake views — continental and Nepali fusion menu featuring duck confit, wild mushroom risotto, and a selection of Himalayan cheeses

day_by_day.notes: The transition from mountain to city can feel abrupt — take the afternoon slowly. The resort offers a full spa menu; book treatments for tomorrow morning. Pokhara's lakeside area (Lakeside/Baidam) is safe for evening strolls.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise flight or private helicopter charter over the Annapurna range from Pokhara airport — a breathtaking aerial perspective of the peaks you just trekked beneath (subject to weather clearance). Alternatively, a sunrise viewpoint drive to Sarangkot Hill for panoramic Himalayan views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full-day leisure in Pokhara. Options include: a private guided kayaking session on Phewa Lake, a visit to the International Mountain Museum (world-class mountaineering exhibits), or a relaxing resort spa session with a 2-hour Himalayan hot stone massage.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with Pokhara's top chef — learn to prepare authentic Nepali dishes including dal bhat, momo dumplings, and aloo tama (bamboo shoot curry). Followed by dining on your own creations.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet: fresh pastries, eggs station, fruit, yogurt, Nepali specialties, and freshly pressed juice
meals.lunch: Lakeside café lunch: avocado toast, Caesar salad, and freshly squeezed pomegranate juice
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations — momos, dal bhat, and aloo tama — paired with Nepali Kukri rum cocktails (non-alcoholic options available)

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights over Annapurna are weather-dependent and require a minimum of 2 guests. Confirm with the resort concierge the evening before. The International Mountain Museum is open 9 AM–5 PM and is highly recommended for context on the peaks you just visited.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Pokhara. Visit the Bindhyabasini Temple (a sacred hilltop Hindu shrine) for a morning blessing and panoramic city views. Browse Lakeside's boutique shops for high-quality Nepali handicrafts, pashmina shawls, Thangka paintings, and handmade jewelry as premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Pokhara to Kathmandu (either by scenic mountain flight — 25 minutes — or private vehicle — 6 hours via Prithvi Highway with scenic stops). If time allows in Kathmandu, a brief visit to Boudhanath Stupa or Pashupatinath Temple for a final cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Kathmandu's finest restaurants — Dwarika's Hotel's Krishnarpan restaurant (traditional Nepali fine dining in a heritage setting) or Kaiser Café in the Garden of Dreams. Final reflections on an extraordinary 14-day Himalayan journey.

meals.breakfast: Resort farewell breakfast: full à la carte menu — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside or in-flight snacks during transfer — premium packed lunch box with sandwiches, fruit, chocolate, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Kathmandu fine dining farewell: Krishnarpan multi-course Nepali tasting menu at Dwarika's Hotel — Nepal's most prestigious heritage dining experience, featuring recipes from royal Nepali kitchens

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and ensure all trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) are retained as souvenirs. Kathmandu airport requires arrival 3 hours before international departure. Your trip coordinator will arrange a final luxury airport transfer. Pack trekking boots in checked luggage — they may trigger security checks if carry-on.
